question: Which age group gets the largest share of new sexually transmitted infections worldwide?
explanation: Young people experience the highest rates of new infections due to a combination of biological and social factors during these formative years. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h1)

question: A 16-year-old girl visits a clinic in Nigeria for a routine check-up. Based on general health trends, what should the midwife focus on most?
explanation: Early adolescence often marks sexual debut, making proactive education and screening vital preventive steps for this age group. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h1)

question: What natural feature of the adolescent female cervix makes it more vulnerable to certain infections?
explanation: Cervical ectopy exposes delicate columnar cells to the vaginal environment, making it easier for bacteria and viruses to enter target tissues. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why do social and economic disadvantages often lead to higher STI rates among young girls?

options.B: They directly alter vaginal pH levels
options.C: They reduce power to negotiate safe sex
options.D: They stop the body from producing antibodies

explanation: Lacking financial independence or social standing often limits an adolescent's ability to insist on condom use or leave risky partnerships. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of these infections is caused by a single-celled parasite rather than a bacterium or virus?
explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by Trichomonas vaginalis, a single-celled protozoan parasite, unlike chlamydia and gonorrhoea which are bacteria. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the main difference in how we treat bacterial versus viral sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Bacterial infections always require lifelong daily suppression
options.B: Viral infections vanish without any form of medical care
options.C: Bacterial infections are generally curable with antibiotics
options.D: Viral infections respond completely to standard penicillin

explanation: Bacterial pathogens like those causing gonorrhoea or chlamydia can be eradicated using targeted antibiotic therapy, whereas viruses persist in the body. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why can it be risky to rely only on physical complaints when checking adolescents for sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Adolescents never experience pain in the pelvic region
options.B: Physical signs only appear in patients over age forty
options.C: Many common infections are entirely asymptomatic
options.D: Symptoms always disappear within twenty-four hours

explanation: Infections like chlamydia often show no visible warning signs, meaning infected youth feel completely healthy while the disease progresses. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h4)

question: A young female client reports painful urination and lower tummy discomfort. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Assure her the symptoms will resolve independently
options.B: Perform a thorough history and physical assessment
options.C: Prescribe broad-spectrum surgery for the pelvis
options.D: Report her diagnosis immediately to school authorities

explanation: Evaluating symptoms through a comprehensive history and exam helps guide appropriate diagnostic testing and clinical management. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is strict privacy so important when offering sexual health care to teenagers?

options.A: It guarantees that laboratory results are always negative
options.B: It replaces the need for any diagnostic testing procedures
options.C: It prevents the spread of airborne respiratory illnesses
options.D: It encourages young people to seek timely medical care

explanation: Adolescents fear social stigma and parental reprisal; knowing their information is private makes them much more willing to visit clinics. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which common laboratory test checks urine or swab samples to detect chlamydia and gonorrhoea?
explanation: Nucleic acid amplification tests offer high sensitivity and specificity for identifying bacterial genetic material in non-invasive samples. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main clinical goal of notifying sexual partners when someone is treated for an STI?

options.A: To prevent reinfection and break transmission cycles
options.B: To confirm the laboratory technician's diagnosis
options.C: To collect extra consultation fees for the clinic
options.D: To penalize individuals who engage in casual sex

explanation: Treating the index patient alone fails if untreated sexual partners continue passing the pathogen back and forth. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h6)

question: When planning partner notification for an adolescent, what should the midwife prioritize above all?

options.A: The safety and confidentiality of the adolescent
options.B: Public posting of names on community boards
options.C: Delaying treatment until partners pay hospital bills
options.D: Involving extended family members in all decisions

explanation: Because partner disclosure can sometimes trigger domestic friction or violence, protecting the young person's physical safety is paramount. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h6)

question: What serious condition can happen if untreated bacterial infections travel up into the upper reproductive tract?
explanation: Pelvic inflammatory disease occurs when pathogens travel upward from the cervix and vagina, infecting the endometrium, fallopian tubes, and pelvic cavity. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h7)

question: How do untreated lower genital infections lead to fertility problems later in young women?

options.A: By shrinking the overall size of the uterine muscle
options.B: By destroying all normal vaginal flora permanently
options.C: By permanently stopping the ovaries from producing eggs
options.D: By causing scarring and blockage in the fallopian tubes

explanation: Tubal scarring obstructs the pathway for sperm and egg to meet, which directly causes tubal factor infertility. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h7)

question: When is the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine most effective for young girls?

options.A: After menopause has completely ended menstruation
options.B: During the third trimester of a first pregnancy
options.C: Only after a confirmed diagnosis of cervical cancer
options.D: Before sexual debut and exposure to the virus

explanation: Vaccinating youth prior to their first sexual encounter provides maximum protection before they encounter the virus. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of youth-friendly health services in midwifery practice?

options.A: To force parents to attend every routine medical visit
options.B: To replace standard hospital wards with children's toys
options.C: To eliminate the need for any laboratory testing equipment
options.D: To remove barriers and encourage youth to seek care

explanation: Youth-friendly spaces reduce judgment, maintain privacy, and make adolescents feel comfortable accessing preventive education and treatment. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T4#BMP320_U3_T4_h8)
